CFML Language Reference: Functions

RandRange

Returns a pseudo-random whole number between two integers, including both end points.

Category

Mathematical functions

Syntax

RandRange(number1, number2)

Parameters

number1
One end of the range (an integer).
number2
The other end of the range (an integer).

Returns

An integer from number1 to number2 inclusive.

Usage

The arguments may be given in either order. Use Randomize first if you need a repeatable sequence. Handy for rotating banner ads, tip-of-the-day boxes and dice games.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Tips = "Bookmark this page!,Upgrade to Netscape 4.7.,Y2K is just around the corner.,Use CFQUERYPARAM.">
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>You rolled: #RandRange(1, 6)# and #RandRange(1, 6)#
<P>Tip of the day: <I>#ListGetAt(Tips, RandRange(1, ListLen(Tips)))#</I>
</CFOUTPUT>
<!--- Roll 600 dice and count the results --->
<CFSET Counts = ArrayNew(1)>
<CFSET ArraySet(Counts, 1, 6, 0)>
<CFLOOP INDEX="i" FROM="1" TO="600"><CFSET r = RandRange(1, 6)><CFSET Counts[r] = Counts[r] + 1></CFLOOP>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Face</TH><TH>Count (of 600)</TH></TR>
<CFLOOP INDEX="f" FROM="1" TO="6">
<CFOUTPUT><TR><TD ALIGN="CENTER">#f#</TD><TD ALIGN="RIGHT">#Counts[f]#</TD></TR></CFOUTPUT>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>
